column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “the assembly of the LORD”; BSB names it once and leaves it implicit in the second clause.
The Hebrew repeats “the assembly of the LORD” and explicitly adds “forever”; BSB names the assembly once and does not include “forever.”
The Hebrew has “bread” and changes from plural “they did not meet” to singular “he hired”; BSB says “food” and continues with plural “they.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says not to seek “their peace and their good”; BSB says not to seek “peace or prosperity from them.” The Hebrew also adds “forever” after “all your days.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes going out as a camp or army; BSB describes being “encamped.”
The Hebrew calls the cause an “occurrence of the night” and separately prohibits entering the camp; BSB specifies “a nocturnal emission” and says to “stay outside.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says to go outside to the designated place without explicitly stating the purpose; BSB supplies “relieve yourself.”
The Hebrew names a peg and says to sit outside and then turn back; BSB has “a digging tool,” “relieve yourself,” and no separate turning action.
The Hebrew names “the nakedness of a thing”; BSB says “anything unclean.”
The Hebrew explicitly repeats “his master” as the one from whom the slave escapes; BSB leaves that source implicit.
The Hebrew names “one of your gates”; BSB uses “the town.”
The Hebrew gives separate prohibitions for the daughters and sons of Israel; BSB combines them into one statement.
The Hebrew distinguishes a prostitute’s wages and “the price of a dog”; BSB combines them as wages of a prostitute, “whether female or male.”
The Hebrew repeats “interest” with money, food, and everything lent at interest; BSB states “interest” once.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly repeats “the LORD your God”; BSB uses “He” for the second occurrence.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says to keep and do what leaves the lips and names a “freewill offering”; BSB says to “follow through” and expresses willingness with “freely vowed.”
The Hebrew says “according to your soul” and uses the general term “your vessel”; BSB has “eat your fill” and specifies “your basket.”
Close to the Hebrew.
